nodes.name: Emergent Fractional Dimensionality And Spinor-Like Holonomy Paper
nodes.statement: The paper idea.md predicts fractional effective dimensionality and spinor-like holonomy for multi-sheeted pentagon tilings, which experiment.mac tests numerically.

sources.heading: Experiment Summary: Multi-Sheeted N-Gon Tilings
sources.quote: for the paper _Emergent Fractional Dimensionality and Spinor-Like Holonomy in Multi-Sheeted Pentagon Tilings_ (`idea.md`)

nodes.name: Medium Preset Signed-3 Configuration
nodes.statement: The run used the medium preset with the signed3 vortex rule for N_GON=5 with BFS_DEPTH=3, M_WALKS=1000, T_STEPS=60, T_CA=16, KPM_MOMENTS=128, KPM_SAMPLES=16, LONG_LOOP_MAX=7, and dense eigendecomposition enabled.

sources.quote: used the **`medium`** preset with the **`signed3`** vortex rule for $N\_GON = 5$

nodes.name: Signed-3 BFS-Grown Multi-Sheeted Pentagon Cluster
nodes.statement: Starting from a single origin pentagon, BFS expansion to depth 3 under the signed-3 vortex rule constructs a 156-cell multi-sheeted graph in exact Q(sqrt(5)) arithmetic.

sources.heading: 1. Cluster Construction (Sections 1–3)
sources.quote: BFS expansion to depth 3 under the **signed-3** vortex rule produced

nodes.name: Medium-Preset Signed-3 Depth-3 Experimental Run
nodes.statement: experiment.mac runs constructive numerical experiments on the signed-3 multi-sheeted pentagon cluster to estimate effective, walk and spectral dimension, holonomy, CA behavior and distance statistics.

sources.quote: `experiment.mac` performs _constructive numerical experiments_ on concrete instances of the multi-sheeted n-gon graph

nodes.name: Cluster Occupies 7 Sheets With 156 Cells
nodes.statement: The signed-3 depth-3 cluster has 156 cells, 155 edges, 103 vortex edges (0.665 fraction), occupies 7 sheets from -3 to 3, and is bipartite on chirality with 26 up and 130 down pentagons.

sources.heading: 1. Cluster Construction (Sections 1–3)
sources.quote: Vortex fraction | 0.665

nodes.name: Cluster Is Bipartite On Chirality
nodes.statement: Every edge in the signed-3 depth-3 cluster connects an up-chirality pentagon to a down-chirality pentagon, with zero same-chirality edges detected.

sources.heading: 1. Cluster Construction (Sections 1–3)
sources.quote: every edge connects "up" to "down" pentagons (0 same-chirality edges detected)

nodes.name: Laplacian Spectral Gap And Eigenvalue Range
nodes.statement: The full Laplacian spectrum of the 156-node cluster has smallest positive eigenvalue 0.02656, largest eigenvalue 9.162, and passes symmetry and row-sum checks.

sources.heading: 2. Spectral Analysis (Section 4)
sources.quote: **Spectral gap** (algebraic connectivity) | $0.02656$

nodes.name: Dense-Eigenvalue DOS Spectral Dimension Estimate
nodes.statement: The dense-eigendecomposition spectral-CDF estimate of the spectral dimension for the depth-3 cluster is 1.907, and is judged the most reliable spectral-dimension value for the run.

sources.heading: 2. Spectral Analysis (Section 4)
sources.quote: Spectral-CDF $d_{\text{spec}}^{\text{DOS}}$ | **1.907**

nodes.name: BFS Volume Growth From Origin
nodes.statement: Cumulative BFS volumes from the origin are N(<=0)=1, N(<=1)=6, N(<=2)=31, N(<=3)=156.

nodes.name: Interior-Fit Effective Dimension Estimate
nodes.statement: A log-log fit of BFS volumes over r in [1,2] gives an interior effective dimension of approximately 2.369 with prefactor C=6.0.

sources.heading: 3. BFS Volume Growth: Connectivity Dimension
sources.quote: **Interior fit** ($r \in [1,2]$): $d_{\text{eff}} \approx 2.369$

nodes.name: Full-Range Effective Dimension Estimate
nodes.statement: A log-log fit of BFS volumes over r in [1,3] gives a full-range effective dimension of approximately 2.901.

sources.heading: 3. BFS Volume Growth: Connectivity Dimension
sources.quote: **Full-range fit** ($r \in [1,3]$): $d_{\text{eff}} \approx 2.901$

nodes.name: Predicted Fractional Effective Dimensionality Window (2,3)
nodes.statement: The paper's construction predicts that the effective dimensionality of multi-sheeted pentagon tilings lies strictly between 2 and 3.
nodes.notes: Inferred from the experiment's framing of the prediction rather than a direct quote of the theory itself; the theory lives in idea.md, not experiment.md.

sources.heading: 3. BFS Volume Growth: Connectivity Dimension
sources.quote: Both estimates lie inside the paper's predicted fractional window $2 < d_{\text{eff}} < 3$

nodes.name: Predicted Sub-Diffusive Spectral Dimension
nodes.statement: The paper predicts that vortex-mediated sub-diffusion causes the spectral dimension to be strictly less than the effective dimension.

sources.heading: Conclusion
sources.quote: consistent with the paper's prediction $d_{\text{spec}} < d_{\text{eff}}$ for vortex-mediated sub-diffusion

nodes.name: Random Walk MSD And Return Probability Slopes
nodes.statement: 1000 walks of length 60 give an MSD early-time slope of 0.262 implying d_w approximately 7.62, a late-time slope near -0.017, and a P0 early-time slope of -1.407 implying d_spec approximately 2.81, both judged boundary-saturated artifacts.
nodes.notes: Values explicitly flagged by the notes as finite-size/boundary-saturation artifacts.

sources.heading: 4. Random Walks
sources.quote: MSD early-time slope | 0.262 ⇒ $d_w \approx 7.62$

nodes.name: Alexander–Orbach Direct-Vs-Predicted Mismatch
nodes.statement: The Alexander-Orbach relation 2 d_eff/d_w evaluates to 0.622 against a direct spectral estimate, a discrepancy of 2.19, attributed to finite-size truncation of the diffusive regime.

sources.heading: 4. Random Walks
sources.quote: Direct vs. AO discrepancy | $2.19$

nodes.name: BFS Depth 3 Causes Boundary Saturation Of Dynamic Statistics
nodes.statement: At BFS radius 3 random walkers, distance catalogs and pinwheel statistics saturate the cluster boundary almost immediately, truncating diffusive and asymptotic regimes.

sources.heading: 4. Random Walks
sources.quote: with BFS radius 3 the walker saturates the cluster almost immediately, truncating the diffusive regime

nodes.name: No Cycles Or Holonomy Detected At Depth 3
nodes.statement: Under the signed-3 rule, the 3-cycle search through the origin found no cycles (girth greater than 8), the length 4-7 long-cycle enumeration also found zero cycles, and the cluster is locally tree-like with 0 triangles and mean clustering coefficient 0.0.

sources.heading: 5. Holonomy (Sections 8, 12, 16)
sources.quote: the **3-cycle search through origin returned no cycles** (girth $> 8$ through origin)

nodes.name: Does Genuine Holonomy Appear At Larger BFS Depth?
nodes.statement: It is unclear whether genuine spinor-like or anyonic holonomy under the signed-3 rule requires BFS depth 4 or greater to produce cycles.

sources.heading: 5. Holonomy (Sections 8, 12, 16)
sources.quote: To observe genuine spinor/anyonic holonomy with this rule, the `large` preset (BFS 4+) is required.

nodes.name: Cellular Automaton Panel Survey Results
nodes.statement: A panel survey of 15 outer-totalistic CA rules on the cluster found 9 extinct, 6 still-life, and 0 periodic, growing or active rules, with B2/S12 the most active non-degenerate rule and 0 gliders/oscillators found in a 25-trial glider hunt.

sources.heading: 6. Cellular Automata (Sections 9, 10, 15)
sources.quote: The glider hunt (5 rules × 5 seed shapes, 25 trials) found **0 oscillators** and **0 gliders** on this small cluster

nodes.name: Signed Vortex Rules Maximize Sheet Count
nodes.statement: Across twelve compared tau-rules at BFS depth 3, the signed-3 and signed-n rules each produce 7 sheets while all other rules produce 4 sheets, with identical cell count 156 and mean degree 1.99 for every rule.

sources.heading: 7. Alternative $\tau$-Rules and Holonomy Comparison (Section 11)
sources.quote: The **signed-3** and **signed-n** rules tie for the most sheets (7); all other rules produce 4 sheets.

nodes.name: Erdős Distance Catalog Shows Strong Boundary Effects
nodes.statement: Among 12090 pairwise squared distances in the 156-cell cluster there are 12195 distinct values, 0 high-multiplicity rings, 0 Galois conjugate pairs, 0 Pythagorean triples, and a D(P_n)/log n ratio of 2415, far above the expected O(1) for the pentagonal lattice.

sources.heading: 13. Erdős Distance Catalog (Section 23)
sources.quote: The very large $D(P_n)$ ratio (expected $O(1)$ for the pentagonal lattice) indicates strong boundary effects

nodes.name: First Six Distance Webs Are Degenerate
nodes.statement: The first six distance webs W_k all share an identical degenerate structure of 34 edges and 129 components because near-zero algebraic residuals collapse the first six distance classes at this scale.

sources.heading: 14. Distance Web Analysis (Section 24)
sources.quote: The first 6 distance webs $W_k$ all share identical degenerate structure (34 edges, 129 components)

nodes.name: No Pinwheel Phenomenon Detected
nodes.statement: None of the first 8 examined distance classes exhibit pinwheel structure; each has a maximum angular gap of 1.85 rad, well above the pinwheel threshold of about 0.628 rad.

sources.heading: 15. Pinwheel Phenomenon (Section 25)
sources.quote: No pinwheel detected.

nodes.name: Commute-Time Log-Log Slope Is Shallow
nodes.statement: Commute-time estimates from the origin to targets at BFS distance 1-3 fit a log-log slope of approximately 0.50, shallower than the slope greater than 1 expected for an extensive fractal with d_w greater than 2.

sources.heading: 16. Commute-Time Sampling (Section 21)
sources.quote: Log-log slope $\approx 0.50$.

nodes.name: KPM Integrated-DOS Spectral Dimension Estimate
nodes.statement: KPM with 128 Chebyshev moments and 16 samples gives mu_0 approximately 1.0 and an integrated-DOS log-log slope of approximately 0.131, implying a KPM spectral dimension of approximately 0.26, quantitatively low due to a rescaling bound warning.
nodes.notes: The notes explicitly flag this estimate as unreliable due to the rescaling warning.

sources.heading: 10. KPM Spectral Density (Section 18)
sources.quote: $$d_{\text{spec}}^{\text{KPM, CDF}} \approx 0.26,$$

nodes.name: KPM Rescaled Spectral Bound Exceeds [-1,1]
nodes.statement: The rescaled spectral bound lambda_max over kpm_b is approximately 1.43, slightly exceeding the valid range [-1,1], triggering a warning that kpm_b should be increased for cleaner DOS reconstruction.

sources.heading: 10. KPM Spectral Density (Section 18)
sources.quote: a warning was emitted; for cleaner DOS reconstruction on this cluster, `kpm_b` should be increased

nodes.name: Intra-Sheet Diffusion Is Faster Than Full Diffusion
nodes.statement: 100 intra-sheet walks of length 60 give an MSD slope of 0.603 implying d_w_intra approximately 3.31, a ratio of 0.435 against the full-graph d_w, and a mean of 39.9 sheet crossings (0.666 per step) per 60-step walk.

sources.heading: 11. Per-Sheet Walk Diagnostics (Section 19)
sources.quote: **Two-thirds of all walker steps cross a sheet** — vortex edges dominate transport completely under signed-3.

nodes.name: Large Or Huge Preset Required For Reliable Estimates
nodes.statement: The notes hold that quantitatively reliable dimensional, holonomy, glider and Erdős-catalog estimates require the large or huge preset at BFS depth 5 or more, rather than the medium preset used here.

sources.heading: Conclusion
sources.quote: For publication-quality dimensional estimates and meaningful holonomy / glider / Erdős statistics, **the `large` or `huge` presets at BFS depth $\ge 5$ are required.**
